==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:trak//tracke<ety:uder<fro:trac>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|trak}}, {{m|enm|tracke}}, from {{der|en|fro|trac|t=track of horses, trail, trace}}, of uncertain origin. Likely from a {{der|en|gem}} source, either {{der|en|non|traðk}} {{gloss|"a track; path; trodden spot"; > {{cog|is|traðk|t=a track; path; tread}}, {{cog|fo|traðk|t=track; tracks}}, {{cog|no|tråkke|t=to trample}}}} or from {{der|en|dum|trec}}, {{m|dum|*trac}}, {{m|dum|treck}} {{gloss|"line, row, series"; > {{cog|nl|trek|t=a draft; feature; trait; groove; expedition}}}}, {{cog|nds-de|Treck|t=a draught; movement; passage; flow}}. See {{m|en|tread}}, {{m|en|trek}}.

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}
[[File:2013-05-10_08_59_55_View_east_along_the_Batona_Trail_through_a_mini-thicket_of_pine_saplings_east_of_Norlemon_Road_in_Brendan_T._Byrne_State_Forest.jpg|thumb|A track between trees (sense 4).]]

# A mark left by something that has passed along.
#: {{syn|en|trace|trail|wake}}
#: {{ux|en|Follow the '''track''' of the ship.}}
#: {{ux|en|Can you see any '''tracks''' in the snow?}}
# A [[mark]] or [[impression]] left by the foot, either of man or animal.
#: {{syn|en|footprint|impression}}
#: {{ux|en|The fox '''tracks''' were still visible in the snow.}}
# The entire lower surface of the foot; said of birds, etc.
# A road or other similar beaten path.
#: {{syn|en|path|road|way}}
#: {{ux|en|Follow the '''track''' for a hundred metres.}}
# Physical course; way.
#: {{syn|en|course|path|trajectory|way}}
#: {{ux|en|Astronomers predicted the '''track''' of the comet.}}
# A path or course laid out for a race, for exercise, etc.
#: {{syn|en|course|racetrack}}
#: {{ux|en|The athletes ran round the '''track'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|The going is good on the '''track'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=IV|page=58|passage=The Celebrity, by arts unknown, induced Mrs. Judge Short and two other ladies to call at Mohair on a certain afternoon when Mr. Cooke was trying a trotter on the '''track'''. The three returned wondering and charmed with Mrs. Cooke; they were sure she had had no hand in the furnishing of that atrocious house.}}
# The direction and progress of someone or something; path.
# {{lb|en|railways}} The way or [[rails]] along which a train moves. {{C|en|Rail transportation}}
#: {{syn|en|rails|railway|train tracks|tracks}}
#: {{ux|en|They briefly closed the railway to remove debris found on the '''track'''.}}
# A [[tract]] or [[area]], such as of land.
#: {{syn|en|area|parcel|region|tract}}
# {{lb|en|slang}} The [[street]], as a [[prostitute]]'s place of work.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Pimpin' Ken|title=PIMPOLOGY: The 48 Laws of the Game|page=11
|passage=A real pimp is a gentleman, but these are pimps in gorilla suits. They hang around pimps, they have hoes on the '''track''' working for them, they may even look like pimps, but they are straight simps.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Paul D. Jones|title=Twilight Nights: The Trials and Tribulations of the Game|page=130
|passage=After putting Tonya Down on the '''track''', we headed to this club called the Players Club.}}
# [[awareness|Awareness]] of something, especially when arising from close [[monitor]]ing.
# {{lb|en|automotive}} The [[distance]] between two opposite [[wheel]]s on a same [[axletree]].
#: {{syn|en|track width}}
# {{lb|en|automotive}} {{ellipsis of|en|caterpillar track}}.
# {{lb|en|cricket}} The [[pitch]].
#: {{syn|en|ground|pitch}}
# Sound stored on a [[record]].
#: {{syn|en|recording}}
# The physical track on a [[record]].
#: {{syn|en|groove}}
# {{lb|en|music}} A [[song]] or other relatively short piece of [[music]], on a [[record]], separated from others by a short silence.
#: {{ux|en|My favourite '''track''' on the album is "Sunshine".}}
# {{lb|en|computing}} A circular (never-ending) data storage unit on a side of magnetic or optical disk, divided into [[sector|sectors]].
# {{lb|en|uncountable|sports}} The [[racing]] events of [[track and field]]; track and field in general.
#: {{syn|en|athletics|track and field}}
#: {{ux|en|I'm going to try out for '''track''' next week.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1973|journal=University of Virginia Undergraduate Record
|passage=The University of Virginia belongs to the Atlantic Coast Conference and competes interscholastically in basketball, baseball, crew, cross country, fencing, football, golf, indoor track, lacrosse, polo, soccer, swimming, tennis, '''track''', and wrestling.}}
# A [[theme]]d set of [[talk]]s within a [[conference]].
# {{lb|en|fashion|colloquial}} {{clipping of|en|trackshoe}}.
# {{senseid|en|Philippines}} {{lb|en|Philippines|education}} A [[specialization]] in [[senior high school]]. Some tracks consist of {{l|en|strand|strands|id=Philippines}}.

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# To continue over time.
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[observe]] the (measured) state of a person or object over time.
##: ''We will '''track''' the raven population over the next six months.''
##* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:Men's Health|year=2026|issue=2|volume=41|title=The Most Important Health Metric You're Not Tracking|author=Ginny Graves|page=18
|text=Your sleep score is consistently high, you're '''tracking''' macros like it's your job, and you've finally got your VO2 max and heart rate variability dialed in.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[monitor]] the movement of a person or object.
##: {{ux|en|Agent Miles has been '''tracking''' the terrorist since Madrid.}}
##* {{RQ:Bramah Eyes of Max Carrados|passage=I always had a suspicion that Calico, with his blend of simple faith and gipsy blood, had violated a temple, or looted a shrine, to save his son's life, and that the guardians of the relic '''tracked''' him and revenged the outrage.}}
##* {{quote-av
|en
|date=May 5, 2022
|author=w:Erin Burnett
|title=See how gamers are outwitting and helping to kill Russian soldiers
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220513115921/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b166ecyNBCw
|archivedate=13 May 2022
|publisher=w:CNN
|time=3:37
|text=Vlad says there is an American drone the Russians can't '''track'''. He wants a lot more of those.}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[match]] the movement or change of a person or object.
##: ''My height '''tracks''' my father's at my age, so I might end up as tall as him.''
## {{lb|en|transitive|or|intransitive|of a camera}} To travel so that a moving object remains in shot.
##: ''The camera '''tracked''' the ball even as the field of play moved back and forth, keeping the action in shot the entire time.''
## {{lb|en|intransitive|chiefly|of a storm}} To move.
##: ''The hurricane '''tracked''' further west than expected.''
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[traverse]]; to move across.
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1837|author=Elizabeth Parker|title=Popular Poems. Selected by E. P.|page=228
|passage=I've swept o'er the mountain, the forest and fell, / I've played on the rock where the wild chamois dwell; / I have '''tracked''' the desert so dreary and rude, / Through the pathless depths of its solitude; {{...}}}}
## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[tow]]. <!--Chambers 1908; compare "track-road" entry-->
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To exhibit good cognitive function.
##: ''Is the patient '''tracking'''? Does he know where he is?''
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|author=Catherine Anderson|title=Blue Skies|publisher=Penguin|isbn=9781101209912|page=39
|passage=''Bess already knew about the painkillers and alcohol not mixing well.... "I wasn't '''tracking''' very well."''}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[follow]] the tracks of.
#: {{ux|en|My uncle spent all day '''tracking''' the deer, whose hoofprints were clear in the mud.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To discover the location of a person or object by following traces.
#: {{ux|en|I '''tracked''' Joe to his friend's bedroom, where he had spent the night.}}
#*: "She could be at any hospital...she could be ill. It's not clear whether she has fled," he told reporters. "Yingluck has many homes and many cars. It is difficult to '''track''' her."
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To make tracks on or to leave in the form of tracks.
#: {{ux|en|In winter, my cat '''tracks''' mud all over the house.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|or|intransitive}} To create a musical recording (a track).
#: {{ux|en|Lil Kyle is gonna '''track''' with that DJ next week.}}
## {{lb|en|computing|transitive|or|intransitive}} To create music using [[tracker]] software.
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2018|author=Dafni Tragaki|title=Made in Greece: Studies in Popular Music
|passage=At the time, '''tracking''' chiptunes (i.e. using trackers) was the fundamental method of chipmusic-making.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|colloquial}} To [[make sense]]; to be consistent with known information
#: {{syn|en|check out|figure}}
#* {{quote-av|en
|year=1988
|title={{w|Dynasty (1981 TV series)|Dynasty}}
|season=8
|number=15
|episode=The Rifle
|text=Vitron isn't hiding anything. The oil is there, the books are open, everything '''tracks'''.
}}
#* {{quote-av|en
|year=2002
|title=w:Without a Trace
|season=1
|number=10
|episode=Midnight Sun
|text=Before he took off, our guy went online... to transfer all his personal accounts into his checking account. CDs, money market funds, everything. That '''tracks'''. According to Nick, he was trying to sell the dry cleaners.
}}
#* {{quote-av|en
|year=2019
|title={{w|Manifest (TV series)|Manifest}}
|season=1
|number=13
|episode=Cleared for Approach
|text=There was an electrical storm in the center of this blizzard, Ben. It's extremely rare, but it can happen. Dark lightning? I can't prove it, but it '''tracks'''.
}}
# To separate into educational tracks, each of which teaches to a different level of ability.
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=4 Feb 90|volume=17|number=29|journal=Gay Community News|page=19|author=Leonard Tirado|title=Privatized 'Recovery' Versus Collective Action|text=Most working class kids are purposely "'''tracked'''" through schools, kept uninformed about scholarships and remedial education/vocation programs and shepherded into dead-end jobs.}}
